title: Chess, But I Can Place Mines On the Board
summary: Minesweeper-inspired chess vs Stockfish. Before the game the player secretly places 3 mines on any empty squares. Any piece that steps on a mine explodes: the piece is lost and the square is destroyed (becomes a permanent hole that can't be moved onto or through). The engine does not know where the mines are. Narrator mines c6, d6 and f6; the engine loses a bishop on d6 and a knight on f6, and White converts the two-piece advantage to a win.
rules: Before move 1 the player places exactly 3 mines on any empty squares; they are hidden from Stockfish.
Any piece (either colour) that moves onto a mined square explodes: the piece is removed and the square is destroyed.
Destroyed squares are permanently off the board: no piece may move onto or through them (sliders blocked, pawns can't use them).
Mines are not triggered by jumping over (knight/pawn double-step passed over d6? 'pawn to D5, jumping directly over the mine' - a pawn double step over a mined square does NOT trigger it).
Otherwise standard chess; player White vs Stockfish (3600).
